title: Implement lazy loading architecture with load_tools meta-tool
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires splitting tools into core (always-loaded, <=1100 tokens, 8-14 tools) and lazy groups (loaded on demand). Currently all 66 tools load on every request, wasting tokens. What needs to be done: Design core group (8-14 most common tools). Organize remaining tools into lazy groups by entity (sites, devices, alerts, jobs, audit, variables, system). Implement rmm_load_tools meta-tool that activates a group for the session. Add tool_not_loaded error when a lazy tool is called before load_tools. Update server.ts to gate lazy tool registration. Target: core manifest <=1100 tokens.

title: Implement standard JSON error envelope {ok: false, error, detail, code}
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires all errors to return {ok: false, error: machine_code, detail: human_message, code: http_status}. Current tools return markdown error strings that Claude cannot act on programmatically. Required error codes: entity_not_found, validation_error, tool_not_loaded, auth_error, rate_limited, permission_denied, duplicate_detected. What needs to be done: Add error mapping layer in apps/mcp-server/src/utils/response.ts. Map all upstream API errors to standard codes. Add rate_limited handling that returns structured error and does NOT auto-retry. Update all tool handlers.
close_reason: All 23 tool handlers (10 Tier 2 + 13 Tier 1 composite) migrated to JSON envelope. 97/97 tests passing.

title: Implement standard JSON response envelope {ok, data, count, next_page, _enhanced}
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires all tool responses to return a structured JSON envelope {ok: true, data, count, next_page, _enhanced} instead of markdown text. Current tools return unstructured markdown strings which skills cannot reliably parse. What needs to be done: Refactor apps/mcp-server/src/utils/response.ts to produce the standard envelope. Update all 66 tool handlers in apps/mcp-server/src/tools/ to return structured data instead of rendered markdown. Add _enhanced field population for all search/get responses that return IDs. Update tests.
close_reason: All 23 tool handlers (10 Tier 2 + 13 Tier 1 composite) migrated to JSON envelope. 97/97 tests passing.

title: Rename all tools: add rmm_ prefix and use underscores
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires all tools to follow {prefix}_{verb}_{entity} naming with underscores. Current tools use hyphens and no prefix (e.g. get-account-dashboard). This causes collisions in multi-product sessions (Autotask + RMM + IT Glue all in the same Claude session). What needs to be done: Rename all 66 tools in apps/mcp-server/src/tools/index.ts from kebab-case to rmm_{verb}_{entity} underscore format. Update the Rust MCP server in crates/mcp-server/src/ to match. Update any tests and documentation that reference tool names.
close_reason: All 66 tools renamed from kebab-case to rmm_ prefix with underscores, applied to TS server, Rust server, tests, and docs.

title: Create governance.md with tool safety classifications
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires every MCP server to ship a governance.md tagging every tool with its safety classification (READ, WRITE, UPDATE, DESTRUCTIVE) and the recommended agent policy. Currently there is no such document. What needs to be done: Create governance.md in apps/mcp-server/ listing all 66 tools with their classification. Document agent policy per classification: READ=always safe, WRITE=preview+confirm, UPDATE=show diff+confirm+patch only, DESTRUCTIVE=explicit approval+impact display+audit log. Also update tool descriptions for write tools to say 'Show preview and confirm before calling.'

title: Write MCP system prompt with trigger map and ordering rules
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires every MCP server to ship a system prompt (<=300 tokens) that carries shared context Claude needs at session start: tool group overview, ID resolution ordering rules, write confirmation rules, error handling rules, and the lazy-loading trigger map. Without this, Claude infers workflow from tool descriptions alone, wasting tokens on repeated guidance. What needs to be done: Write system prompt for the Datto RMM MCP server. Include: tool group listing, trigger phrases mapped to lazy groups, ordering chain (resolve siteUid before deviceUid), write confirmation requirement, rate_limited handling rule. Add it to apps/mcp-server/src/server.ts.

title: Add _enhanced ID resolution to all search and get responses
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires _enhanced on every response that contains an ID, resolving it to a human-readable name (e.g. companyName, assignedResourceName). Without this, Claude makes extra lookup calls just to resolve IDs. What needs to be done: For every search and get tool response in apps/mcp-server/src/tools/, populate an _enhanced field with resolved human-readable names for all IDs in the response. Common cases: siteUid -> siteName, deviceUid -> hostname, alertUid -> alert title. Cache lookups where possible within a single tool call.

title: Add duplicate_detected check on all create tools
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires all create tools to check for an existing matching record before writing and return error: 'duplicate_detected' if found. Currently create-site, create-account-variable, create-site-variable, and create-quick-job have no duplicate detection. What needs to be done: For each create tool in apps/mcp-server/src/tools/, add a pre-write lookup to detect duplicates. On match, return {ok: false, error: 'duplicate_detected', detail: 'A record with this name already exists', code: 409} along with the existing record. Do not write.

title: Add token budget CI test - core manifest <=1100 tokens
description: Why: The Kaseya MCP Best Practices standard requires a CI-gated test that fails the build if the core tool manifest exceeds 1100 tokens. This prevents token cost regression as tools are added. What needs to be done: Install @anthropic-ai/sdk as a dev dependency in apps/mcp-server. Write tests/token-budget.test.ts that calls anthropic.messages.countTokens() against the core tools manifest and asserts input_tokens < 1100. Add it to the test suite in package.json. Depends on lazy loading issue being done first (need to define core group).
